name: Foxtech Babyshark 260 VTOL
description: The Foxtech Babyshark 260 VTOL, a 2.5 m quadplane (four lift rotors on two booms, a pusher propeller, an inverted V-tail), for the threepp examples. One file holds every number: the published flight model (babyshark_rig.py runs it), what the thesis does not give and the rig needs to fly from a hover to the cruise and back (marked ASSUMED or OURS, with the reason), the layout the Blender generator builds on (build_babyshark_blender.py -> babyshark.glb), and the controller's gains.

thesis.author: Bernhard Paus Graesdal
thesis.title: Full Nonlinear System Identification for a Vertical-Takeoff-and-Landing Unmanned Aerial Vehicle
thesis.kind: Master's thesis, Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU), 2021
thesis.licence: Neither repository carries a licence file. The model repository's README asks that the thesis be cited by whoever uses the model, and says that porting it is straightforward since every equation and parameter is in its BabysharkModel.m. So: the equations and the numbers are taken and cited; no code is copied (babyshark_rig.py is written from the thesis's equations (6.6)-(6.16)), and the repository's 3D model (babyshark.stl) is not used or redistributed: babyshark.glb is built here from the thesis's own geometry file and figures.
thesis.use: The flight model in babyshark_rig.py is the thesis's equations (6.6)-(6.16) as written, with the numbers of its Tables 6.2 (airframe), 6.3 (actuators), 6.4 (aerodynamic coefficients, here at the full precision the model repository's BabysharkModel.m carries; the table prints them rounded) and 6.5 (trim), copied unchanged into the blocks `physical`, `actuators`, `aero` and `trim`. Its linear matrices (6.17), (6.18) and modes (Table 6.7) are in `thesis_linearisation` for the comparison. Nothing in those blocks is tuned.
thesis.identified_at: Flight tests in fixed-wing flight around 21 m/s, the lift rotors stopped: 2-1-1 manoeuvres of about 5 s on each control surface, flown on PX4 (a Pixhawk 2.1), with no wind assumed. Stepwise regression (equation error) for the model's structure, then the output-error method for its numbers. The propellers were identified on a thrust stand with no incoming air (thesis Figs. 4-5, 4-6), the servos with a high-speed camera, the inertia from a CAD model with the weighed parts.
thesis.not_identified: The thesis says so itself (its section 7.1.1): nothing near the stall (the lift never declines in its data, which reach alpha = 16 deg), no flight on the lift rotors (their model is the thrust stand's), no transition, no wind, no change of the propellers' thrust with airspeed. Its phugoid and spiral modes are not to be trusted (the manoeuvres are too short to show them).

airframe.figures: Foxtech's own figures, as resellers and sUAS News repeat them: wingspan 2.5 m, frame 2.68 kg, 5.5 kg without batteries, maximum take-off 12 kg, payload 6.5 kg with the batteries, stall speed 15 to 16 m/s, top speed about 100 km/h, up to 2.5 h. Manufacturer's claims, none of them independently tested; the rig is not fitted to any of them and compares itself with the stall and top speeds (babyshark_flight.py --checks).
airframe.geometry_source: No drawings are public. The lifting surfaces are the thesis author's own measurements of the airframe, as his vortex-lattice input writes them (identification repository, avl_model/avl_model/vtol.avl: wing sections, the tail's panels, the reference point); the rotor axes are the thesis's Table 4.3; everything else (fuselage, booms, landing gear, motors) is fitted by eye to the thesis's Figs. 3-1, 3-2 and 4-1.

units: SI: m, kg, s, N, rad unless a key says deg. Propeller speeds are in rev/s, as in the thesis (its inputs delta_t and delta_MR are the SQUARED rev/s).

frames.body: The thesis's: x forward, y right, z down, origin at the centre of gravity. NED position (n, e, d), zyx Euler angles (phi, theta, psi), body velocity (u, v, w) and rates (p, q, r).
frames.layout: The .glb's and the `layout` block's: X forward, Y up, Z right (starboard), metres, origin at the centre of gravity (the thesis's body origin). A body vector (x, y, z) is (x, -z, y) in it.
frames.avl: The thesis author's vortex-lattice file measures x aft from the nose, y right, z up, with the centre of gravity at (0.494, 0, -0.043) (its vtol.mass). Layout X = 0.494 - x_avl, Y = z_avl + 0.043, Z = y_avl.

physical.S_note: the wings AND the tail projected on the x-y plane of the author's CAD model (thesis 4.2.3), not the wing alone. On the model built here the wing and the tail project to 0.715 m^2, and to 0.659 m^2 with what the pod covers left out, 0.4 % from the thesis's figure: the thesis seems to count the exposed surfaces
physical.J_note: from the author's CAD model with the weighed parts spread over it (thesis 4.2.2). The model repository's code carries the eight Gamma constants of Table 6.2 as numbers; computed from these four inertias they agree to the fourth digit (babyshark_flight.py --checks 1)

mass_table.note: The table prints a quantity of 2 for the pusher motor; its total of 12.140 kg is met with 1 (with 2 the rows sum to 12.490), and the aircraft has one pusher.

aero.source: thesis Table 6.4, eqs. (6.8), (6.10), at the precision of the model repository's BabysharkModel.m
aero.note: The rates are made non-dimensional with the TRIM airspeed, not the current one: p^ = b p / (2 V*), q^ = cbar q / (2 V*), r^ = b r / (2 V*) (eq. 6.11). The control surfaces enter as their deflections away from the trim (eq. 6.13), except in the rudder-pitch coupling cmdr2, which takes the rudder's own deflection squared (eq. 6.10b; the trim rudder is zero). (6.8e) prints cL's elevator term without the Delta; the model repository's code, and the static curves (6.19), take the deflection away from the trim, and so does the rig.

trim.source: thesis Table 6.5 (and 4.5): found in manual flights with an RC pilot, not solved from the model
trim.eta_fw_note: The tables print the trim throttle as 125 rev/s squared. The model repository's code sets 110 squared ('just some throttle that keeps the aircraft mostly at constant altitude', its example says), and the recorded inputs it ships sit near delta_t = 9750 (98.7 rev/s) before a manoeuvre. The model's own level flight at 21 m/s needs 18.4 N of thrust: babyshark_flight.py --checks 3 prints what that is in each reading.
trim.note: The trim point is not an equilibrium of the model: with every surface at its trim and alpha = theta = 3 deg, the lift is 9 % more than the weight (w' = -1.0 m/s^2). The rig's own trim (Babyshark.trim) solves the equations; this block is what the surfaces' deflections are measured from, and V is the V* of the non-dimensional rates.

actuators.servo_note: eq. (3.41): a first-order response of T_servo held inside the rate limit, the same for the four servos; the surface stops at its maximum. delta_a, delta_e, delta_r are the aileron, elevator and rudder the autopilot's mixer makes of the two ailerons and the two ruddervators (eq. 3.40): the model has no ruddervators of its own.
actuators.propeller_note: T = rho D^4 cT n^2 and Q = rho D^5 cQ n^2, n in rev/s (eqs. 6.15): thrust-stand fits with no incoming air. Fixed wing: T-Motor AT4120 500KV, 15x8 wood; multirotor: T-Motor MN505-S 320KV, 16x5.5 carbon (Table 4.4).

rotors.note: Table 4.3: each lift rotor's place from the centre of gravity, body x (forward) and y (right); the thesis takes no height (its moments (6.14) have none). spin: +1 for a rotor whose torque on the airframe is positive about body z, that is one turning counter-clockwise seen from above (eq. 3.46: Q1 + Q2 - Q3 - Q4). PX4's quadrotor-X order.

thesis_linearisation.source: thesis eqs. (6.17), (6.18) and Table 6.7: the model linearised at the trim of Table 6.5, the lift rotors out, for the comparison in babyshark_flight.py --checks 2. Longitudinal state (u, w, q, theta), input (delta_e, delta_t); lateral state (v, p, r, phi), input (delta_a, delta_r).

propulsion.note: What the thesis does not give and a flight from a hover to the cruise needs. ASSUMED or OURS, each with what it rests on. Nothing here enters the thesis's equations at the conditions it identified them in: with no incoming air the pusher's thrust is the thesis's own, and the lift rotors' thrust in a still hover is the thesis's own.
propulsion.eta_fw_max_note: rev/s. The top of the thesis's thrust-stand run of the pusher (its Fig. 4-5 ends at 142 rev/s, 45 N), taken as full throttle. ASSUMED to be that
propulsion.J0_fw_note: OURS and ASSUMED: the thesis's static law does not lose thrust to the airspeed (it names an advance-ratio model as future work, section 7.1.1). Here T = rho D^4 cT n^2 (1 - J / J0), J = V_x / (n D) the advance ratio on the air's speed along the shaft: the thesis's law at J = 0, falling in a straight line to nothing at J0. J0 = 0.80 is 1.5 times the 15x8 propeller's pitch over its diameter, where such propellers' thrust reaches zero. Not fitted to anything; what it predicts is compared in babyshark_flight.py --checks 3 (the thesis's trim throttle, the product page's top speed)
propulsion.cQ_fw_note: read off the thesis's Fig. 4-5 (about 1.03 N m at 142 rev/s; the thesis fits no torque coefficient for the pusher and neglects its torque on the airframe, which its aileron trim and cl0 carry). Used for the battery's power only, as the static value at every airspeed: the cruise power is not to be quoted
propulsion.tau_fw_note: first-order lag of the pusher's speed on its command, s. ASSUMED
propulsion.eta_mr_max_note: rev/s: 54 N a rotor by the thesis's static law, a thrust-to-weight ratio of 1.8 for the lift system. ASSUMED: quadplanes of this class are sized at 1.5 to 2. The thesis's thrust-stand run of the lift propeller ends at 99 rev/s (33 N, its Fig. 4-6), which is 11 % over the hover and cannot be the motor's limit at the flight voltage; beyond 99 rev/s the static law is extrapolated
propulsion.eta_mr_idle_note: rev/s the lift rotors turn at when armed on the ground and never fall below in a hover. ASSUMED
propulsion.tau_mr_note: first-order lag of a lift rotor's speed on its command, s. ASSUMED: what 16 in propellers on such motors show (0.04 to 0.08)
propulsion.inflow_note: OURS and ASSUMED, the model of m350_rig.py: a lift rotor's thrust is the thesis's static one less kz n v_ax, v_ax the air's speed through the disc (positive when the disc climbs through the air), kz from blade-element and momentum theory with this mean chord and section lift slope. In a still hover it is the thesis's law exactly; it is what damps a climb, a roll and a pitch in the hover
propulsion.h_force_note: OURS and ASSUMED: each lift rotor's in-plane force, H = -kh n v_perp with kh = 2 pi rho sigma cd0 A R / 4 from blade-element theory (the profile drag of the advancing and retreating blades), acting at the rotor's hub (in the plane of the centre of gravity, as the thesis places the rotors). Small: about 0.1 N a rotor at 15 m/s
propulsion.drive_efficiency_note: shaft power over battery power (motor, speed controller, wiring). ASSUMED
propulsion.avionics_note: what the aircraft draws beside the motors. ASSUMED
propulsion.battery_note: ASSUMED from the thesis's mass table and Foxtech's suggested set-up (two 6S packs for the lift motors, 30 to 40 Ah for the cruise motor): the two 6.5 Ah packs in series feed the four lift motors (320 KV motors are 12S motors), the three 11 Ah packs in parallel feed the pusher (a 500 KV motor on 6S). The thesis names capacities and masses only
propulsion.not_modelled: The propellers' gyroscopic moment and the pusher's torque on the airframe (the thesis neglects both: its section 3.5.2); the lift rotors' gain of thrust in forward flight (translational lift) and what their wake does to the wing and the wing to them in the transition (a wind-tunnel study of a quadplane found more drag and less thrust there: A. Mathur and E. Atkins, arXiv:2301.12316); ground effect; the stopped lift propellers' drag is in the identified cD, a turning one's is the H force above

envelope.source: OURS, not the thesis's: what the model does outside the range it was identified in. Inside it the thesis's equations are untouched.
envelope.alpha_note: The flight data of the thesis's Fig. 6-12 span alpha -13..+16 deg (cL -0.9..+1.7), and the lift never breaks in them. Inside this range the coefficients are the thesis's.
envelope.beta_note: ASSUMED: the thesis shows no sideslip range; its lateral manoeuvres are 2-1-1 steps on the aileron and the rudder about straight flight.
envelope.blend_note: ASSUMED. Past either range the forces and moments go over, on a smoothstep across this many degrees, from the thesis's coefficients (evaluated at the range's edge) to the bluff body below: a stall that the thesis's data do not contain and it says a quadratic lift cannot give ('a combination between a linear and a flat-plate model is expected to work well', its section 7.1.1). With it the lift peaks at the edge of the data (cL 1.64 at alpha = 16 deg) and falls from there. What flies inside the range never sees it; the hover, the transition's first seconds and the back transition's last do
envelope.va_min_note: The thesis's code sets alpha and beta to zero below 1 m/s of airspeed; the rig keeps the angles (atan2) and the bluff body takes over there anyway, since alpha and beta are whatever the hover's drift makes them

bluff.note: ASSUMED: the airframe as a bluff body where the wing does not fly, the model m350_rig.py uses for the whole Matrice: F = -0.5 rho Cd |v| (A_front v_x, A_side v_y, A_top v_z) in body axes, each part at its own centre of pressure, so a descent pitches the nose down a little (the tail is behind the centre of gravity) and a sideways drift turns the nose into the air (so does the real aircraft: PX4 calls it weathervaning). Areas and centres are measured on the model's meshes (build_babyshark_blender.py --check: everything but the propeller blades seen along X, Z and Y, rasterised on a 2 mm grid, and each silhouette's centroid); --write-areas writes the three areas here
bluff.drag_coefficient_note: a flat plate broadside on (1.17 to 1.28 for these aspect ratios)
bluff.cp_note: layout frame (X forward, Y up, Z right), from the centre of gravity: the centroid of each silhouette. Top: the wing (0.575 m^2 on the mesh, centroid 0.08 m behind the centre of gravity), the tail (0.140 m^2, 0.87 m behind), the pod and the booms. Side: the pod, the two tail panels seen from the side and the booms

environment.g_note: the thesis's (its code and its mass file)
environment.rho_note: The thesis takes rho = 1.225 kg/m^3, a constant (Table 6.3). Here it is the ISA troposphere's density at the aircraft's height above mean sea level, which is 1.225 at the sea: h0 = 0 and a low flight are the thesis's air to within a percent. A number here in place of 'isa' fixes it.

ground.note: The landing gear on the ground (babyshark_rig.py, the contact model of m350_rig.py). All ASSUMED. Contact points: the four feet of layout.gear. Each: a spring and damper along the ground's normal (4 x 10000 N/m carries 12.14 kg on 3 mm of sag at 57 rad/s; 4 x 350 N s/m is its critical damping, so a touchdown does not bounce) and a bristle across it that holds up to friction times the normal force and slides beyond.

wind.note: m350_rig.Wind, which this rig uses as it is: a logarithmic mean profile (or a scene's field) and the low-altitude Dryden turbulence of MIL-F-8785C / MIL-HDBK-1797. The same numbers as m350_spec.json's wind block, which says what each is. The thesis's model has no wind: the rig puts the air-relative velocity where the thesis has the body velocity in the airspeed, alpha and beta (6.12), the standard extension, which the thesis itself names as future work.

autopilot.source: OURS, not the thesis's (its flights flew PX4). The fixed-wing half of babyshark_rig.Autopilot: successive loop closure (Beard and McLain, Small Unmanned Aircraft, ch. 6) as in x8_rig.py: roll on the aileron, pitch on the elevator, course (or heading) on roll, altitude on pitch, airspeed on the pusher, and the rudder holding the yaw rate a coordinated turn has. The inner gains are computed from the thesis's coefficients at the airspeed; what is chosen here is each loop's natural frequency or stiffness, its damping, its integral and its limits. State feedback is EXACT: no estimator, no sensor noise.
autopilot.airspeed_range_note: what command() accepts. The model's slowest steady flight is 15.1 m/s (the elevator's throw ends there; Foxtech gives a stall speed of 15 to 16 m/s), its fastest 22.6 m/s (the pusher at full speed), and it was identified at 21
autopilot.note: roll: kp = wn^2 / a_phi2, rate feedback where the airframe's own roll damping falls short of 2 zeta wn. course: wn = roll wn / bandwidth_ratio. pitch: kp adds `stiffness` times the airframe's own pitch stiffness (kp = stiffness cma / cmde), rate feedback brings the short period's damping (0.39 in the thesis's Table 6.7) to zeta, and an integral (wi rad/s, at most integral_deg of elevator) removes the steady error. altitude: wn and zeta of h' = V theta; a turn's extra load is fed forward (cL / cL_alpha times 1 / cos(phi) - 1); outside +-zone m of the commanded height the pitch command is at its limit; nose up, that limit is the trim's pitch plus climb_fraction of the steepest climb the pusher's thrust at full speed can hold at the commanded airspeed (0.7 m/s at 21 m/s, 1.8 m/s at 17: this aircraft at 12 kg climbs slowly on the wing), so a climb costs height rate and not airspeed. speed: wn and zeta of the airspeed on the pusher's thrust. yaw: delta_r = kr (r - g sin(phi) cos(theta) / V) - kb beta, held inside limit_deg: a yaw damper about the coordinated turn's rate (the dutch roll's damping is 0.19 in Table 6.7) and the exact sideslip fed back, which adds kb cndr / cnb = 1.1 times the airframe's own weathercock stiffness and takes the sideslip of a 30 deg roll-in from 5.6 deg to 4.0.

guidance.source: OURS: x8_rig.LOS, the line-of-sight law on a polyline of waypoints, used as it is (x8_spec.json's guidance block says what each number is).

control.note: OURS, not PX4's code: the multirotor half of babyshark_rig.Autopilot, the cascade of m350_rig.Autopilot (position, velocity, thrust vector inside a tilt limit, attitude, body rates, mixer) with this airframe's inertia and rotor geometry, and the transition between the two halves, laid out as PX4's standard-VTOL transition is (the thesis's aircraft flew PX4, and its section 7.1.2 describes that transition and its loss of height). State feedback is EXACT. Every bandwidth is set against the lift motors' lag (propulsion.tau_mr: 0.06 s, 17 rad/s) from the inside out.

rate.note: angular acceleration = kp (w_c - w) + ki int - kd w', times the inertia: the M350's loop shape, a = 12 rad/s inside the motor's 17 (kp = 2.6 a^2 tau, kd = 2.6 a tau - 1, attitude.kp_tilt = a / 2.6). Yaw has only the rotors' drag torque (an arm of D cQ / cT = 0.026 m against 0.4 m): its loop is slow.

attitude.note: body rates = 2 kp (the vector part of the error quaternion); beyond yaw_accel_rads2 / kp_yaw^2 of yaw error the yaw rate follows the square root of the error. tilt_max_deg bounds the lean a hover may command, yaw_rate_max_dps its turn. ASSUMED limits: Foxtech publishes none

velocity.note: acceleration = feed-forward + kp (v_c - v) + ki int, as in m350_spec.json. The integrals lean the aircraft into a wind it is not told about

position.note: velocity = feed-forward + kp (p_c - p), the speed following the square root of the distance beyond brake_ms2 / kp_xy^2. speed_xy_max_ms bounds a hover's horizontal speed, well under the wing's 15 m/s; climb_max_ms and descent_max_ms its vertical one. ASSUMED limits

weathervane.note: OURS, after PX4's weathervane for VTOLs: in a hover the yaw setpoint turns toward the side the velocity loop's integral leans the aircraft to (the wind it has learned to hold against, not a manoeuvre's lean), at gain_per_s times that sideways lean, once it passes min_tilt_deg. The lift rotors' yaw torque cannot hold the tail across a wind (the bluff body's side force acts 0.23 m behind the centre of gravity). On by default in a hover without a yaw command of its own

transition.note: OURS, laid out as PX4's standard-VTOL transition. Front (hover to wing): the pusher ramps to throttle_front over ramp_s; the multirotor loops hold the height, the wings level and the pitch at pitch_deg while the airspeed builds; from blend_ms the multirotor's moments fade, gone at speed_ms, the surfaces flying the same attitude throughout; at speed_ms the lift rotors are stopped and the fixed-wing loops have it. The height stays on the lift rotors' collective until then: as the wing takes the weight the collective falls to idle by itself. Back (wing to hover): the pusher stops, the lift rotors start, the multirotor loops take the attitude and the height at once and slow the aircraft at decel_ms2; while the wing can still carry the weight, the nose stays pitch_margin_deg under the angle of attack at which it would carry all of it, so braking does not balloon it and the lift rotors keep a little of the weight; below back_speed_ms it is a hover. In both transitions the lift rotors' collective may fall to what they give at idle. speed_ms is 1.19 times the model's slowest steady flight

mission.note: babyshark_rig.Mission. Take-off: spool_s at idle, a vertical climb at climb_ms. A hover leg moves at hover_speed_ms. A cruise leg is a route of waypoints at an altitude and an airspeed, flown with x8_rig.LOS; it begins with a front transition along the route's first leg if the aircraft is hovering, flown level at the height it has (the altitude is commanded once the wing has the aircraft: climbing on the lift rotors while the wing is at a negative angle of attack costs the lift battery twice). A landing begins the back transition back_distance_m before its point along the track (ASSUMED, from the back transition's measured stopping distance with a margin), hovers to the point, comes down at land_rate_ms to land_slow_height_m above the ground and at land_slow_rate_ms below it, and stops the rotors on contact
mission.back_distance_note: the back transition from 21 m/s takes 125 m in still air (babyshark_flight.py --checks 7) and 30 m into 8 m/s; the hover flies what is left

pilot.note: babyshark_rig.Pilot, OURS: four sticks (forward, turn, side, up; each -1..1) on the autopilot's setpoints, the same four hovering and on the wing, modelled on the assisted modes of a VTOL's autopilot. Hovering: forward and side are speeds along and across the nose (position.speed_xy_max_ms forward, back_ms and side_ms the other ways), turn is the yaw rate (attitude.yaw_rate_max_dps, the yaw setpoint never more than yaw_lead_deg ahead of the nose; let go, the setpoint is the nose itself until it turns slower than yaw_stop_dps, so it stops without swinging back), up is the climb rate (position.climb_max_ms and descent_max_ms; under mission.land_slow_height_m the descent is mission.land_slow_rate_ms). The speed setpoint moves at hover_accel_ms2 at most. Sticks at rest it brakes at position.brake_ms2 and holds its place, its height and its heading; once it has held its place under weathervane_speed_ms for weathervane_after_s the weathervane has the nose (not sooner: after a turn at speed the velocity loop's integral still leans the aircraft for some seconds, and the weathervane would follow that). On the wing: turn is the bank (autopilot.roll.limit_deg at transition.speed_ms and faster, shrinking to none at bank_none_ms: the model's slowest steady flight is 15.1 m/s, where the elevator's throw ends, and a level turn banked 30 deg needs 16.2; let go, wings level and, inside level_deg, the course it then has), up moves the height setpoint at autopilot.altitude.climb_fraction of the steepest climb the pusher can hold at this airspeed, or down at wing_descent_ms (the rate itself changing at wing_accel_ms2, so the wing levels off over some seconds and the pull-up does not cost it its airspeed), and forward moves the airspeed setpoint between transition.speed_ms and the top of autopilot.airspeed_range at airspeed_rate_ms2, in steps of airspeed_step_ms (each step designs the wing's gains anew). A key is all or nothing: a stick follows it over stick_time_s. The height setpoint never leads the aircraft by more than height_lead_m (wing_height_lead_m on the wing). On the ground, up spools the lift rotors for mission.spool_s and lifts off; down held for land_hold_s on the ground stops them. All ASSUMED

layout.note: Where things are, layout frame (X forward, Y up, Z right, origin at the centre of gravity). The wing and the tail are the thesis author's vortex-lattice file moved into this frame, unchanged; the rotor axes are the thesis's Table 4.3; the rest is ASSUMED, fitted by eye to the thesis's Figs. 3-1, 3-2 and 4-1, and the model's generator may refine it but must keep its nodes on the rotor axes, the hinge lines and the feet.

wing.note: half wing, mirrored: [X of the leading edge, Z, chord] per section, in the plane Y = y. No dihedral, twist or incidence in the author's file. Airfoil Eppler 397 (the manufacturer's word to the author). Area 0.571 m^2 for both halves

aileron.note: the hinge line, as a fraction of the local chord from the leading edge, at the inner and the outer end

tail.note: an inverted V (an 'A-tail') standing on the two booms: each panel from its foot on the boom up and inward to the flat centre piece. Chord 0.170 throughout, leading edge at X, set at incidence_deg (leading edge up). Airfoil NACA 0010. The ruddervators are the panels' rear 30 %
tail.panel_note: [Y, Z] of the starboard panel's two ends, mirrored to port

boom.note: ASSUMED, the generator's fit to the thesis's renders (model.boom has it all): at Z = +-0.400 (the rotors' and the tail feet's), a moulded arm under the wing from x_front, with a pad under each lift motor, and a round tube from its aft end to the tail, its axis at the tail panel's foot

lift_rotors.note: disc centres. X and Z are the thesis's Table 4.3; Y (the discs above the booms) is ASSUMED and is the 3D model's only: the flight model takes the rotors in the plane of the centre of gravity, as the thesis does. Diameter 0.4064 (16 in), two blades

pusher.note: ASSUMED by eye (Fig. 3-2): the disc just behind the fuselage's end, on its axis. Diameter 0.381 (15 in), two blades; it spins about body +x (clockwise seen from behind), the thesis's section 3.5.2

fuselage.note: ASSUMED, the generator's fit to the thesis's renders (model.fuselage has the sections): a pod under the wing, its nose 0.49 m ahead of the centre of gravity (the vortex-lattice file's origin), its flat end where the pusher motor stands; y is its lowest and highest point

gear.note: ASSUMED, fitted by the model's generator to the thesis's Fig. 4-1 enlarged and scaled by the rotor axes (its bottom view shows two bent-strip frames under the pod at X about +0.19 and -0.17, their feet out to about +-0.18; model.gear has the frames). feet: the four contact points (the pads' undersides) the flight model stands on: the centre of gravity is 0.260 m above the ground, and the pusher's blade tip passes 0.025 m above it

model.note: The 3D model's own numbers (build_babyshark_blender.py), layout frame. The wing's sections, the tail's panels and the rotor axes are the layout's; everything here is fitted by eye to the thesis's renders of the author's CAD model (Figs. 3-1, 3-2, 4-1: a perspective, top, bottom, front and side view), scaled by the rotor axes (0.800 m apart both ways) and the 2.5 m span. The views are perspective renders, so a length read off them is good to about 1 cm. No lettering or logos.

wing.note: The planform is a monotone cubic through the layout's sections (leading and trailing edge each), so it meets every section and has no corners between them; the layout's 0.571 m^2 is the straight-line area. section: the NACA four-digit thickness form on a four-digit camber line, standing in for the Eppler 397 (its coordinates are not reproduced here; thickness and camber by eye). tip_slope: the leading edge's slope at the tip as a multiple of the last two sections' (3 is the most a monotone cubic takes): a round tip. tip_round: the span over which the section thins to the tip's edge. aileron_gap: between the aileron's ends and the wing

tail.note: ruddervator_span: where the ruddervator is, as fractions of the panel from its foot (Figs. 3-1, 3-2). The centre piece runs straight from each panel's top (Y 0.343 at Z +-0.100) to centre_y on the centreline (0.340), the three points the layout gives: a sag of 3 mm over its 0.2 m. foot_extension: how far the panel runs on into the boom's tube

fuselage.note: The pod: its nose at nose_x on the height nose_y, its flat end at end_x (a circle about the pusher's axis, where the motor stands). half_width, top, bottom: tables over X, tail to nose, before the nose's rounding; the nose is an ellipse of nose_length in each (a blunt nose from the side, a longer one from above). A section is two superellipse halves (exponent above, below) meeting at the widest point, widest_at of the height down from the top: an egg, the wide end up, as the front view shows; from tail_blend_x aft it goes over to the circle. 0.197 wide and 0.182 high (the layout's 0.170 and 0.195 were read off the small figures)

boom.note: Each boom is a moulded arm under the wing (white, widening to a pad under each lift motor, a round front end) and a round tube from its aft end to the tail: a white sleeve, bare carbon, a white fitting along the tail panel's foot with a round end. fairing: [X, half width, half height, centre Y] along the arm, aft to front, before the front end's rounding (an ellipse of fairing_nose). The tube's axis is at the tail panel's foot (layout.tail.panel_foot's Y), 0.018 above the layout's by-eye boom.y. saddle: a strip that fills the gap between the arm's top and the wing's underside toward the leading and trailing edges

lift_motor.note: T-Motor MN505-S (thesis Table 4.4), a plain black can standing on the arm's pad as in the renders: base_y and can_y from the pad up. The diameter and height are the motor's catalogue size as remembered (56 x 31 mm), not looked up

lift_propeller.note: 16 x 5.5 in carbon, two blades (thesis Table 4.4); the diameter is actuators.D_mr. Chord and thickness along the blade by eye, f = 0 at root_r, 1 at the tip. hub_y: the hub's ends from the disc centre

pusher_motor.note: T-Motor AT4120 (thesis Table 4.4): a black can on the pod's end, about the pusher's axis; radius and length read off the renders

pusher_propeller.note: 15 x 8 in wood, two blades (thesis Table 4.4); the diameter is actuators.D_fw. Chord and thickness by eye for a wooden propeller of that size; hub_x: the hub's ends from the disc centre

gear.note: Two frames under the pod, each one bent strip: across the belly, down and out to a knee, a flat foot outward with a turned-up lip, a rubber pad under the foot. x: the two frames' stations. knee: [Y of the strip's centre line, Z]. The pads' undersides are layout.gear.feet

pitot.note: the thesis names a pitot tube at the nose (its section 4.1); the renders show none

gnss.note: the thesis names an external GNSS and magnetometer on the outside of the airframe; the renders show none. A puck on the pod's back behind the wing

sensors.note: the empties: position (and what a camera looks along). ASSUMED, all of them

imu.note: the flight controller, in the pod near the centre of gravity

camera_nadir.note: a downward camera in the belly, the usual survey payload; the image's top toward the nose

camera_fpv.note: a forward camera in the nose, under the pitot tube

gates.note: what --check fails the build on. Lengths in m. span: [value, tolerance] over the wing's mesh. lift_axis: each lift node and its motor can from layout.lift_rotors in X and Z. tip circles: [value, tolerance]. tail_ends: the leading edge at the panel's foot and top from layout.tail's, in Y and Z; tail_leading_edge: in X. feet: the pads' undersides from layout.gear.feet. clearance: the least gap a rotor disc must keep (seen from above for the lift discs against the wing, the tail and each other; in its own plane for the pusher against the booms, and down to the feet's plane)

model.unverified: Not seen in the renders, or not to be read off them: the wing's section (a stand-in for the Eppler 397), its thickness, and any twist or dihedral (the vortex-lattice file has none); how the wing blends into the pod (it passes through the pod's top here, with no fillet); the arm's section and how it meets the wing's underside; the motors' real shapes (plain cans here), their mounts and the propellers' hubs and blade shapes; the pitot tube, the GNSS puck and both camera windows (none is in the renders: the thesis's text names the first two, the cameras are ours); hatches, seams, servo horns and hinge gaps (the surfaces are cut clean at the layout's hinge lines); the ailerons' extent (the layout's 0.557 to 1.089 is the vortex-lattice file's; Fig. 3-2 draws them from about 0.48 to 0.95); the gear's strip section; the colour of anything but the white airframe, the dark tail tubes and the black motors. Foxtech's product photographs were not consulted

materials.note: name: linear base colour, metallic, roughness. ASSUMED from the thesis's renders: a white gloss airframe, satin carbon tail tubes, black motors; the propellers as the thesis's Table 4.4 names them (carbon on the lift motors, wood on the pusher). No vendor marks
